entries.description: Operator set pathAwareCritique: required.
Register.

**Adopt `pytest-xdist`.** Add the dependency, make parallel execution the documented default in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and in `run_of_record.py`'s recorded pytest command. **Prove parity before adopting**: identical passed/skipped counts serial vs parallel, and record both timings. If any test proves parallel-unsafe, fix or mark it — do not abandon the change for one offender.

**Correct every published test timing.** `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "~30s" and "~90s for ~10 scenarios" are wrong by up to 30x; sweep for the same figures elsewhere. Cite the measurement and its commit so the next reader can re-derive it.

**Record `durationSeconds` as a structured field** in `test-runs.jsonl`, written by the same helper that records the run. A free-text `detail` that sometimes mentions minutes is not a measurement. Add it to `verification_stamp.py`'s bookkeeping exclusions **in this session** — Session 2 owns the reasoning, but a new writer must not ship un-excluded.
Full pytest (parallel) at close after freeze; verify, close.
Register.

Adopt pytest-xdist: added to pyproject.toml tests extra, wired as pytest.ini addopts -n auto (single point of truth for local/CI/run_of_record). Parity already proven on this machine/commit lineage (docs/test-suite-benchmark-DENICI.txt: 3769 passed / 5 skipped both serial 845.76s and -n auto 234.55s); reconfirmed on a targeted subset post-change.

Corrected CONTRIBUTING.md Layer 1 (~30s -> ~14min serial/~4min parallel, cited benchmark) and Layer 3 (~90s for ~10 scenarios -> ~9.6min median across 33, cited Sets 111-114 test-runs.jsonl detail fields). Swept repo for the same stale strings; only CONTRIBUTING.md carried live/current claims -- historical session-set specs, changelogs, and the benchmark script itself (which cites the old figures as its own motivation) were left untouched.

Added duration_seconds field to TestRunRecord/record_run/read_records in run_of_record.py (durationSeconds in JSON, optional, validated positive), wired --duration-seconds into the record CLI. Added test-runs.jsonl to verification_stamp.WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING (freshness-exempt, same class as decisions.jsonl/checklist-posts.jsonl) but NOT to EVIDENCE_VISIBLE_BOOKKEEPING (its content is redundant with disposition.json, which is also hidden). New tests in test_run_of_record.py cover the duration field and the freshness/evidence split.
Full pytest (-n auto) run after last code change: 3808 passed, 5 skipped in 245.46s (0:04:05). Recorded via run_of_record (duration_seconds=245.46). Proceeding to verify_session and close.

Discovery round 1: 3 Major/Completeness findings (missing e2e-specific timing, parity evidence not proven on the reviewed tree, durationSeconds optional at the writer boundary). All accepted and remediated: measured the real -m e2e command (113.69s serial/63.47s parallel, 8 tests); recorded a same-tree serial/parallel pair (matching surfaceDigest b5db7d2d776d, 3813 passed/5 skipped both ways, 647.01s/240.56s) and cited it in CONTRIBUTING.md; made --duration-seconds required on the record CLI plus a NaN/Infinity/bool validation fix (both fanout calls raised it independently). Sidecar: s1-remediation-round-1.md.

Round 2 (remediation-review) rejected all 3 round-1 fixes, all correctly. Root cause of L1/L2: test-runs.jsonl was excluded from EVIDENCE_VISIBLE_BOOKKEEPING, so the verifier could never see the parity/timing evidence it was asked to corroborate -- moved it there (joining decisions.jsonl/checklist-posts.jsonl on identical reasoning). L3: record_run() itself (not just the CLI) now requires duration_seconds (Python keyword-only required arg); ~15 internal test call sites updated to pass a fixed duration_seconds=1.0 where duration was not the thing under test. Sidecar: s1-remediation-round-2.md.

Round 3 (remediation-review cycle 2) hit the enforced bound with L1/L2 still rejected (L3 accepted). Operator authorized one more round via AskUserQuestion (journaled in decisions.jsonl). Checked in two raw pytest-transcript evidence files (s1-e2e-parity-benchmark.txt, s1-full-suite-parity-benchmark.txt) mirroring the DENICI benchmark format; all 4 underlying runs (e2e serial/parallel, full serial/parallel) share the identical surfaceDigest fb69075938a4, cryptographically proving one tree. CONTRIBUTING.md now links both files directly. Sidecar: s1-remediation-round-3.md.
Register.

**Put every route under one budget.** `close_backstop.py:554` resolves a round with no bounds while `verify_session.py` enforces them. Unify them: one cap covering `verify_session` rounds, backstop rounds and the discovery fan-out. **Stop on a clean result**; never encode a round *quota*.

**Refuse deterministically at the cap.** The backstop must not silently buy rounds 5-12. At the cap it stops and says what it wants — an operator waiver or an adjudication — exactly as `verify_session` already refuses.

**Make backstop rounds auditable.** Every round it runs is written to `sN-rounds.jsonl` like any other, so the ledger is the true count. Add a test that a backstop round past the cap cannot proceed unauthorized, and a regression test that recording the final test run does **not** stale a passed verification.
Full pytest at close after freeze; verify, close.

close_backstop now evaluates evaluate_phase_bound(phase=None) before any metered call -- same function, same arithmetic, same PHASE_BOUND_CLASSIC as verify_session. A backstop round is an unphased round and consumes the classic budget; no second allowance invented. Placed AFTER the settling-evidence skip so a clean session still closes.

New STATUS_ROUND_BOUND_REACHED + _round_bound_remediation() naming the two EXISTING operator exits (close_session --manual-verify, verify_session --operator-authorized-round); wired into close_session gate-failure mapping so the close blocks rather than buying rounds 5-12.

Backstop rounds now append round-completed to sN-rounds.jsonl with a source field (reusing verification_stamp STAMP_SOURCES, not a second vocabulary); ledger added to written_paths and to _settling_bookkeeping_paths (the I-084-S2-9 sibling, L-069-1) so it does not trip working_tree_clean on the run or the rerun. gate_checks._checklist_transitions now skips backstop-sourced rounds -- they run DURING the close, so their post window opens after the last moment anyone could post. 15 new tests: bound refusal + look-alikes, ledger/source auditability, checklist non-transition + look-alike, staleness end-to-end + narrowness look-alike, and 3 fan-out one-budget tests.

Appended the Session 2 assignment block: orchestrator recorded as actually run (claude-opus-5, not the recommended sonnet), and the self-judging risk named in advance -- if the new bound fires on this session own close, the correct response is the operator exit, never widening the cap.
Registered session 2 via start_session (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5, effort high); preload read; transport profile api with all three DABBLER_* keys present; no decision-review-queue entries.

Frozen, then: full pytest 3829 passed / 5 skipped in 255.58s (parallel), and full Layer 3 Playwright 36 passed in 11.7m (owed because close_session.py is on the playwright covers list). Both recorded with durations. Verification round 1 (discovery, 2-lens fan-out) VERIFIED from both lenses, zero Critical/Major, anthropic excluded, $0.78. Two record-level nits fixed; three adjudicated-minor residuals journaled and carried in the disposition.
Register. **Confirm Set 114 is complete** (it was, 2026-08-10 08:40) and read what it shipped before editing `gate_checks.py`.

**Operator decision, journaled.** Reducing gates is a verification reduction and sits inside the decision-rights hard carve-out; it is never self-authorized. **The operator ruled on 2026-08-10 — see [`operator-notes.md`](operator-notes.md) for the per-gate disposition.** That is direction; this step still records the attestation in `decisions.jsonl` at the time of implementation, and confirms the ruling still stands before acting on it.

**Implement the ruling.** Keep `verification_integrity`, `uat_walk_recorded` and `test_run_fresh` as gates. Keep `working_tree_clean` and `pushed_to_remote` as **transactional preconditions** — they protect the write, not the ceremony. **Delete nothing.** **Demote to warn-not-block** `checklist_posted`, `activity_log_entry`, `next_orchestrator_present`, `change_log_fresh` and `verification_method_vocabulary`: each check still runs and still prints, but it cannot refuse a close.

**Fix what "a fresh test run" means — and when it happens.** Two halves of one bug. **(a)** `test_run_fresh` does not govern pytest: `pytest` and `mocha` are `expensive=False` in `run_of_record.py`, which is why a session could run 15 suites unremarked. Scope it to the surfaces the session actually touched, so a docs-only session never owes Playwright. **(b) Move the full-suite run from Step 5 to Step 8** in `docs/session-constitution.md`. Step 5 today says expensive suites run *"fully once, after the last code change"* — but **Step 7 remediation is a code change**, so the instruction is unsatisfiable in any session where verification finds anything, which is nearly all of them. Targeted tests during the loop; **one applicable full run after remediation, before close.** This depends on Session 2's staleness fix and must not ship before it.
Close: `change-log.md`, the **required** path-aware critique, Step 9 review; verify, close.

Registered session 3 (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5, effort high). Read the four preload files. Confirmed Set 114 COMPLETE (all 3 sessions VERIFIED, terminal close 2026-08-10T08:40) and read its change-log.md before touching gate_checks.py: 114 shipped the checklist_posted gate + checklist-posts.jsonl ledger, start_session plan-step seeding, the Explorer's fifth tree level, and a fix to check_activity_log_entry so seeded plan rows cannot satisfy it. Appended the Session 3 block to ai-assignment.md (step 3.5) recording the orchestrator choice, the three things this session must not do, and the fact that BOTH prior sessions of this set closed on an operator-attested checklist_posted waiver.

Presented the 2026-08-10 gate ruling as an education-mode brief and got the operator's attestation at the moment of implementation, as the spec requires (operator-notes.md is direction, never the attestation). The brief named three things the ruling did not have in front of it: (1) verification_method_vocabulary is the ONLY close-time enforcement of a legal verification_method token, because validate_disposition's rule 4 is never called at close; (2) the gate-(c) repair is an enforcement INCREASE that has never actually run, since evaluate_freshness already scopes by touched path and only the `expensive` flag was wrong; (3) both prior sessions of this set closed on an operator-attested checklist_posted waiver, which is this set's own evidence for that demotion. Operator chose 'Attest the ruling as written' -- all five demotions, accepting the token-hygiene residual. Journaled to decisions.jsonl with authority=human, rubric_line=verification-reduction, verification_effect=reduces.

Implemented the attested ruling. gate_checks.ADVISORY_CHECKS is the executable form of the table and is_blocking_check() is the single predicate every consumer asks; GateResult carries a `blocking` field so gate_results JSON says which kind each row was. verification_method_vocabulary became its own registry row (appended last, never inserted) and its blocking layer left check_verification_integrity; the --manual-verify substitution in _run_gate_checks collapsed to a plain pass, deleting a second spelling of a check that already runs. Sibling site fixed per L-069-1: session_state.mark_session_complete is the OTHER consumer of the gate verdict and now asks blocking_failures() too, logging advisory failures as warnings. Nothing deleted -- every demoted check keeps its predicate, message and tests. THREE things the tests caught that reading did not: (1) removing the backstop's vocabulary early-out was wrong -- the ruling falsified its stated REASON but not its conclusion, since an unknown token still has no corroboration path, so the skip was restored with corrected reasoning; (2) demoting change_log_fresh exposed a sibling in the state writer -- _flip_state_to_closed required change-log.md to be PRESENT before calling a session the last one, so a final session without one passed the gate chain and then wrote top-status in-progress over an all-complete sessions[], raising SessionStateInvariantError instead of closing (a demotion had turned a clean refusal into a CRASH); the redundant condition was removed and the crash pinned by asserting the flipped state, not just 'succeeded'; (3) an illegal token still cannot pass check_verification_integrity on an ordinary repo -- it falls through to the zero-budget arm -- so the demotion bites only under --manual-verify and on a declared zero-budget repo, which is now asserted from both sides.

Both halves. (a) pytest and mocha are now expensive=True: `expensive` is the flag deciding whether test_run_fresh has an OPINION, not a claim about the clock, and the path-level scoping the operator asked for already existed in evaluate_freshness -- a docs-only session still owes nothing, which is what makes widening affordable. pytest's recorded command also picked up Session 1's `-n auto` default, since a run of record naming the serial command records a run nobody performs. Evidence cited in the code: Set 112 S3's 15 runs / 186 minutes for pytest, and Set 114 S3's two close-gate regressions shipped into the sample project while Layer 2 sat unrun. (b) The full-suite run moved from Step 5 to Step 8 in session-constitution.md, with Step 5 rewritten as targeted-only and the reason stated (Step 7 remediation IS a code change, so the old instruction was unsatisfiable rather than merely ignored). Propagated to every live echo (L-065-1): the authoring guide's test-run policy, its record-command comment, close-out.md's gate list, and run_of_record.py's own docstrings. Historical session artifacts left untouched -- they are records.

Round 1 (discovery, 2-lens fan-out, gpt-5-6-sol both lenses, anthropic excluded, $0.786): VERIFIED from BOTH lenses, zero Critical/Major -- a non-blocking round that opens no remediation loop. Five nits raised; ALL FIVE fixed anyway, because three were places where a doc written this session stated something false about the code beside it, and this set's subject is making the doctrine true. Both lenses converged independently on the two that mattered: (1) 'a docs-only session owes nothing' is FALSE under ai_router/ -- covers is a path PREFIX not a file type, so this session's own edit to ai_router/docs/close-out.md owes pytest; narrowing covers to exempt docs folders was considered and REJECTED (it would make the gate skippable by putting code in a docs-named folder), so the wording was corrected and both sides of the boundary pinned by tests. (2) '--force' was never inside 'every close' -- it runs verification_integrity alone; correct and older than this ruling, so documented rather than changed. Also fixed: the residual was stated more broadly in the gate_checks overview than the code supports (the real exceptions are --manual-verify and a declared zero-budget repo with a matching token) -- the CODE docs corrected, decisions.jsonl deliberately left as written since the brief overstated the exposure rather than understating it and a decision journal records what was said at the time; 'hard fail'/'enforcement point' wording for demoted checks; and the once-per-session rule reworded to bound the RUN OF RECORD rather than curiosity. Fixing after a stamped round stales the stamp, so the close backstop will run one bounded round -- Set 116 S2's own machinery, doing what it was built for. Sidecar: s3-nit-dispositions.md.

Set-terminal close. change-log.md authored covering all three sessions plus the round-1 nit dispositions, the path-aware critique outcome and the Step 9 review. Suites of record taken AFTER the last code change, per the Step 8 ordering this session ships: pytest 3850 passed / 5 skipped (308.08s, -n 8) and Playwright 36 passed (12.1m, owed because close_session.py and session_state.py are both on its covers list). REQUIRED path-aware critique ran with two repo-reading critics: gemini-2.5-pro VERIFIED, gpt-5.4 ISSUES_FOUND with one Major claiming close-out.md's attested-override bullet was false on the actual close path. DISPUTED and put to the operator per the never-re-round-a-disputed-finding rule; dismissed as a false positive on an executable citation (a passing regression test closes the real Set 083 incident disposition on that path and asserts succeeded/passed=False/blocking=False), with its one real grain taken -- the backstop's refusal message now says explicitly that the attested override is a separate invocation which never reaches the backstop. Journaled with the operator's attestation; the decision_journal keyword screen refused two earlier phrasings and the entry records why the flag is named in prose. Step 9: no guidance edits -- both preload files are AT their ceilings, so an addition is an operator budget decision; recommended a new Conventions entry ('demoting a gate is not a local change -- find every sibling of the GUARANTEE you are removing', L-069-1 read backwards) which meets four of five admission criteria and fails only recurrence, one occurrence not being recurrence. checklist_posted fails for this session at 2 transitions and is left UNWAIVED on purpose: it is advisory under the ruling this session shipped, so it warns and the close proceeds -- the first session of three in this set not to need an operator waiver for that gate.
